The thrombin-error passage was removed, but one of its replacements contains a different error. The sp-hemostasis passage says activated platelets 'release their cytoplasmic granules that include ADP, thromboxane A2, serotonin'. TXA2 is not stored in granules: it is made on demand from membrane arachidonic acid by COX-1 and TXA synthase and then diffuses out. The module's own c-cox-1 teaches exactly that. The passage appears in excerpts, so learners see the contradiction. sp-txa2 still fully supports the claim, and the sp-platelet-activation 'TXA2 produced by platelet cyclooxygenase' passage is fine.

Mostly fixed. V and VIII are now correctly called cofactors, and why_here matches. New, minor problem: the text calls II, VII, IX, X, XI and XII 'the enzyme-type clotting factors'. Factor XIII is also a zymogen activated into an enzyme (XIIIa, a transglutaminase that cross-links fibrin). The quoted sp-coag-pathways line ('factors V, VIII, and XIII are not classified as serine proteases') makes it easy for a learner to conclude XIII is a cofactor. The list is correct for serine proteases, not for enzymes generally.
correction: 'The serine-protease clotting factors (II, VII, IX, X, XI, XII) circulate as zymogens and are activated into enzymes; factor XIII is also activated into an enzyme that stabilizes fibrin. Factors V and VIII are not enzymes; they are cofactors.' Mirror the change in why_here.

Not false at glossary level, but 'each activated clotting factor activates the next' (and the definition's 'chain ... each activating the next') is the linear waterfall picture. It is not exact for cofactors (Va and VIIIa do not activate anything) and leaves out thrombin's feedback activation and the platelet-surface (cell-based) setting the app teaches. It is not the Y diagram, so it is not a model violation, but it should carry a simplified flag.
